items.action: Cais das Colunas takes its name from two pillars beside the Praça do Comércio riverfront, designed by Eugénio dos Santos during the rebuilding of Lisbon after the 1755 earthquake.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio
items.place: Cais das Colunas, Praça do Comércio, Lisbon

items.action: The pillars top a marble staircase down to the Tagus; the quay serves as the river gateway into Lisbon, aligned with the equestrian statue of Dom José I and the Rua Augusta arch.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio
items.place: Cais das Colunas, Praça do Comércio

items.action: The quay's construction date is undocumented, but it was finished before the end of the 18th century.
items.conditions: No written documentation on construction date
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio

items.action: The columns were pulled down at the end of the 19th century and put back in 1929.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio

items.action: The columns were dismantled in 1997 for metro extension works to Santa Apolónia and reassembled in 2008.
items.conditions: Metro extension works to Santa Apolónia
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio

items.action: Mud almost covers the base of the two pillars, which bear the names Salazar and General Carmona, making inscriptions hard to read.
items.conditions: Tagus mud covering the pillar bases
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio

items.action: President Carmona boarded a ship at the Cais das Colunas for his first voyage to the overseas colonies, and landed there on return.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio
items.place: Cais das Colunas; São Tomé and Angola
items.who: Óscar Carmona, President of the Republic

items.action: Carmona embarked again at the Cais das Colunas for a second colonial voyage, returning to the same quay.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio
items.place: Cais das Colunas; Cape Verde, Mozambique, Angola
items.who: Óscar Carmona, President of the Republic

items.action: Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom entered Portugal between the two columns when she visited Lisbon in 1957.
items.location: Cais das Colunas - Praça do Comércio

items.action: A commenter recalls fishing at the quay, digging worms in the mud and catching crabs, before an installation whose name is cut off.
